editorial:
You meet Alma, a young nurse assigned to care for Elisabeth, an actress who has stopped speaking even though she seems physically fine. Their quiet time together turns into something strange as Alma talks and talks while Elisabeth only watches. The movie feels close and tense, with long silences, sharp stares, and a growing sense that the two women are becoming tangled in ways neither expected.

The acting is powerful, especially the way small facial changes carry huge weight, and the black-and-white images make every moment feel raw and unforgettable. It moves slowly, so if you want fast action, this may not be your pick. You will need patience, but the payoff is strong. But if you like deep character stories and bold filmmaking, it is worth your time.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Alma discovers Elisabeth has been studying her, which breaks their trust. Their faces and voices begin to overlap, making it unclear where one woman ends and the other begins. Alma eventually leaves the house and the care arrangement, while Elisabeth stays behind. The movie ends with a quiet, unsettling image that suggests the two have shared something deeper than friendship, leaving you to decide how much was real.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves bold character studies and classic black-and-white films.
